title: Domain-Driven Design in .NET
description: Apply Domain-Driven Design building blocks: entities, value objects, aggregates, repositories, and domain events in .NET applications.

data.text: Domain-Driven Design (DDD) provides a set of tactical patterns to model complex business domains. By isolating domain logic from infrastructure concerns, DDD enables teams to build expressive, maintainable, and testable domain models that scale with business complexity. In .NET, these patterns map naturally to classes, interfaces, and dependency injection.

An Entity is defined by its identity, not its attributes. Two Entity instances with the same identity are considered the same object across the lifecycle of the application, even if their properties differ. Entities encapsulate state changes through behavior methods rather than exposing public setters.

data.text: Value Objects derive their identity from their attributes. Two Value Objects with identical property values are considered equal. They are immutable by design, providing thread safety and predictable behavior in distributed systems.

data.text: An Aggregate is a cluster of domain objects that can be treated as a single unit. The Aggregate Root is the entry point through which the outside world interacts with the aggregate. All state changes within an aggregate must go through the root, ensuring invariants are always maintained.

Repositories abstract data access behind collection-like interfaces. They allow the domain layer to query for aggregates by their identity or by specification, without knowing the underlying persistence technology (EF Core, Dapper, MongoDB, etc.).

data.text: Domain Events decouple side effects (logging, notifications, integration) from domain logic. When an aggregate's state changes meaningfully, it publishes a domain event. Event handlers in the infrastructure layer react to these events.

data.text: Use strongly-typed IDs with records or wrapper structs to prevent accidentally passing a CustomerId where an OrderId is expected. This eliminates an entire class of bugs at compile time.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Entities are identity-based; enforce invariants through behavior methods, not public setters
Value Objects are immutable and compared by value — ideal for Money, Address, Email
Aggregates group related objects, with the root enforcing consistency boundaries
Repositories abstract persistence behind collection-like domain interfaces
Domain Events decouple side effects, promoting clean separation of concerns
data.takeaway: DDD tactical patterns bring clarity to complex domains by making business logic explicit, enforceable, and testable through well-defined boundaries.
